summary: Focused retest of (a) Reports Excel/PDF exports and (b) the new Referral Reward Coupon system, plus full backend regression (102 tests) and Playwright UI verification. New suite /app/backend/tests/test_coupons_exports.py (13 tests) — ALL PASS: excel/pdf export magic bytes + content-type + user_id filter + 400 on bad format + 401 unauth; auto-coupon on referral (15%, unused, referred_person_name correct, no _id leak); 2 referrals => 2 independent coupons (%30 total); PATCH used/unused sets & clears used_at/used_by/used_by_name and persists; coupon A used does NOT affect coupon B; delete cascade keeps USED coupons and removes UNUSED ones (both for referred person and referrer); startup backfill creates missing coupons (verified with backend restart, now env-gated); RBAC 403 for consultant on non-assigned person for both GET /persons/{pid}/coupons and PATCH /coupons/{cid}, 200 for admin/assigned consultant; 404 for unknown person/coupon. UI: admin login -> /customers/8cee312f... renders data-testid='referral-coupons' with summary badge '%15 (1 kupon)' / '%30 (2 kupon)', per-coupon rows, confirm dialog on toggle, used state persists after reload, cancel keeps state, toggle-back works. Reports page Excel & PDF buttons download valid xlsx (PK, 4983 B) and pdf (%PDF-), also with consultant filter. Full regression: 99 passed, 3 failed, 2 skipped — the 3 failures are pre-existing auth/RBAC hardening gaps unrelated to this iteration. DB left tidy (1 baseline seed coupon, 0 TEST_ persons/products, login_attempts cleared).

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout is unreliable: login_attempts identifier = f'{request.client.host}:{email}'. Behind the k8s ingress requests arrive from several proxy IPs (observed 10.231.129.137 and .138), so 6 consecutive bad logins split across identifiers and never reach the 5-fail threshold (codes=[401 x6]). Key the counter on email only (optionally combined with X-Forwarded-For first hop).
No httpOnly access_token cookie is set although auth.py falls back to an access_token cookie; token is returned in the JSON body only (frontend stores it client-side). Pre-existing from iteration 1.
Consultant can list all users (200) — user directory is not admin-only. Pre-existing from iteration 1; confirm if intentional (assignment dropdowns) and if so restrict the returned fields.

ui_bugs.issue: Badge is binary: lifecycle_status==='customer' ? 'Aktif Müşteri' : 'Mezun'. A lead (e.g. referrer 8cee312f..., Durum: lead) is mislabeled 'Mezun' in the header while the overview shows 'lead'. Should map lead/customer/graduate distinctly.

integration_issues.issue: toggleCoupon() PATCHes then calls the full load() (12 parallel/sequential API calls) with no optimistic update or pending state; the card can still show the old status for ~2s after the success toast appears (my first 3s assertion caught a stale card while the backend was already 'used'). Consider optimistic setCoupons update or a per-row spinner + disabled button.

issues: 'Doğum Tarihi' uses the native browser date input (mm/dd/yyyy US format) instead of the shadcn calendar / TR dd.MM.yyyy format used elsewhere.
Coupon card itself is well laid out (green=unused / gray=used, contrast OK); no contrast or spacing problems found on Reports page.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout key (use email, not request.client.host, behind ingress).
Decide/fix httpOnly cookie on login (auth.py already reads access_token cookie).
Restrict GET /api/users to admin (or return minimal fields to consultants).
Fix CustomerDetail header badge so leads are not labelled 'Mezun'.
Optional: optimistic update / disabled state for coupon toggle to avoid ~2s stale card.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/server.py is 1635 lines — split into routers (persons, coupons, finance, reports) as suggested previously; a routes/ package already exists but is unused.
Startup backfill iterates all persons with referred_by_person_id on every boot and issues 1 find_one per person; fine now (2 persons) but should be an aggregation/bulk op if data grows.
_create_referral_coupon correctly de-duplicates on (person_id, referred_person_id); consider a unique compound index to enforce it under concurrency.

CORS: allow_origins comes from CORS_ORIGINS which is '*' in backend/.env, so allow_credentials is force-disabled — acceptable for Bearer-token auth, but blocks any future cookie auth; set an explicit origin list if httpOnly cookies are adopted.
